corrected:
User's question: do the three together give +0.01? MEASURED directly: exp60 x138 lab, 56 clips, ins35 base 0.93988, official metric, all edits applied in one graph (LINK -> ATT -> FP):
- Fork removal (O_FP): +0.00629 (44b6 +0.00695, 6bba +0.00577).
- Gated perfect orphan attach (O_ATT_g, 7 TP, all 6bba): +0.00541 (44b6 0, 6bba +0.00634).
- Wide perfect orphan attach (O_ATT_w, 26 TP): +0.02039.
- Linking: strict end -> free start +0.00026; with ID-switch repair (swap) +0.00621; broad O_LINK +0.00734.
- O_FP + O_ATT_g: +0.01339 (44b6 +0.00695, 6bba +0.01375).
- O_FP + O_ATT_g + strict link: ~+0.0137 (additive approximation; 44b6 ~+0.0070, 6bba ~+0.0140).
- O_FP + O_ATT_g + O_LINK: +0.02056 measured (44b6 +0.02354, 6bba +0.02009), div 32/0/67, edge 38543/1505/1550.
- O_FP + O_ATT_w + O_LINK: +0.04115 measured (44b6 +0.03294, 6bba +0.04208).
So the answer is YES, as an oracle: the three together give +0.014 to +0.021 lab on the gated pool, and up to +0.04 on the wide pool. That is more than m_transfer's +0.0135 to +0.0168. Divisions supply 0.0131 of it (gated) and the edge side supplies the rest. Almost all of the 'linking' part is repairing wrong links, not joining free ends. At 1/6 transfer this is +0.0023 to +0.0034 public. The 1/6 is optimistic for the edge-repair part, because edge-side gains transferred at ~0.
The verdict stands: realistic cues (best measured AUC 0.73, precision 3.4%/2.4%, fork removers 0 for 5 on the LB) capture only a few percent of this. 70% of the div oracle needs AUC ~0.99. Nothing is buildable or honestly gateable before R8 (27 Sep 12:00Z), so the finals stay #37 + #38.
